bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/intents.rs (runtime and dispatch), springboard/sdk/src/testing.rs (headless window test kit), springboard/sdk/src/quicksearch.rs (Spotlight index), springboard/src/shell/intents.rs (shell side)
summary: BifrOSt has an App Intents runtime served over the control socket (intent.list, intent.<id>, entity.query) and a headless UI test kit, and the intent dispatch function is public so Rust unit tests can run intents in-process. There is no intent test layer: no catalog type, no typed result or value-query result types, no entity annotation (onscreen context), and no type-erased test wrappers, so tests pass and compare raw JSON.

features.feature: Headless test harness for app UI
features.apple: Test target harness (used by App Intents Testing for in-app checks)
features.note: Clicks, keys and accessibility queries work headless; nothing in it knows about intents or entities

gaps: No intent test helpers: no test session that runs an intent by type and returns a checked result (dispatch() is public but returns raw Json).
No value query results or intent value queries (ResolvedValueQueryResult, IntentValueQueryDefinition).
No entity annotation or onscreen context (ViewAnnotation), so Spotlight and Siri cannot be told what is on screen.
No enum parameter type and no transient entities (AnyAppEnum, AnyTransientAppEntity).
No key-path access to nested intent values (DynamicPropertyPath); tests use string keys.
Intents run in-process in unit tests and only out-of-process through the control socket; there is no separate test runner.
Siri and voice dialog verification is not modelled (see docs/bifrost-ui.md App Intents gaps).
